_comment: Registry of academic presses to track for new releases. Each press has a `source` saying HOW to pull its new titles. type 'sitemap' is the front-line: snapshot-diff the press's own XML sitemap (a new book-URL = a new book), then fetch og:title/og:description per new page. `index` = a sitemap (or sitemap-index to descend); `sitemaps` = explicit urlsets; `book_substr` filters book pages by URL ('' keeps all, for sub-sitemaps that are already all-books); `sub_filter` descends only index sub-sitemaps whose URL contains it ('product' for WordPress presses whose books live in dedicated product sub-sitemaps). type 'loc-backfill' = no usable sitemap found; covered by the LoC SRU + OpenLibrary subject/year paths instead. Crossref was tested and rejected (publisher-name filter is ignored; book dates are dirty). Coverage probed 2026-05-30/31: sitemap front-line live (book-URL counts verified) for princeton (41.8k), chicago (23.5k), columbia (18.6k), cornell (13.2k), yale (12.2k), harvard (7.5k, sub_filter sitemap_books), minnesota (5.8k), stanford (4.6k), washington (2.8k), duke (flat slugs + book_marker 'isbn:' to drop journal issues); loc-backfill for mit, california, oxford, cambridge, routledge.

source.note: mitpress.mit.edu blocks robots/sitemap (Cloudflare 403); covered via LoC/OpenLibrary
flat root slugs mix books with journal issues; book_marker 'isbn:' keeps only book pages (journal issues carry an ISSN, no 'ISBN:' label)
ucpress.edu (Supadu) exposes no sitemap; covered via LoC/OpenLibrary
cambridge.org/sitemap.xml (books at /highereducation/books/) returns HTTP 403 to a non-browser User-Agent; not scraped (no UA spoofing). Covered via LoC/OpenLibrary.
academic.oup.com (Silverchair) exposes no usable book sitemap; covered via LoC/OpenLibrary
